implementation.deadline_scope: One accepted absolute deadline and cooperative service owner, including pre-shape waits, late tightening, handler construction and response commitment.
implementation.unary_accounting_scope: Native unary, client-streaming and Web unary lifecycle accounting uses the actual committed writer Status, including codec and byte-admission errors; later Drop or clock changes do not replace it.
implementation.native_terminal_scope: One terminal result; native error trailers may discard unsent DATA while preserving initial HTTP/2 headers and the current frame length.
implementation.web_terminal_scope: Safe completed-message boundaries preserve base64 carry and status-body framing. An unfinished partial Web BODY frame requires a transport reset; a new body status cannot overwrite missing payload.
implementation.router_scope: Routing selects the existing boxed service future synchronously under the accepted owner, retaining one selected future instead of the full Rpc across an initial Router async state; post-logging and interceptor expiry checks remain explicit.
implementation.router_layout_limit: Private release proof Router4288->544bytes with Single544bytes unchanged; layout is not shipping allocator, CPU, latency, throughput or RSS evidence.
implementation.compression_scope: Fresh gzip encoder per message with one bounded initialized output chunk; level clamp, complete member/trailer validation and writer error handling remain explicit.
limits: Timers cannot preempt synchronous user or codec polls.
No protocol can force output through a blocked TCP socket; Web status DATA also requires peer flow-control credit.
Private pooled records and queued transport bytes are not a universal process-RSS bound.

native.interpretation: Observed counter differences, including tiny/noisy increases, are retained. They are not significance tests or shipping-speed verdicts.
limits: shared-host separate-process diagnostics; qualified=false
synthetic zero-filled payloads and exact selected scopes are recorded in cells; four streaming messages
per-RPC deadlines, readiness and teardown timeouts remain unchanged
no measured scheduling noise, independent host statistics or broad superiority proof

Client-streaming load handlers use tokio::join!(send, call), matching the tonic structure. The producer is not explicitly completed before polling the Call. Queue16 can contain the four messages, but scheduling is not a witness that every oversized capture uses the preclosed fallback.
Oversized captures measure API cases and per-side counters. Controlled independent-peer regressions establish the preclosed-upload mechanism; these captures do not isolate that mechanism.
Each oversized protobuf payload contains1MiB of zeros. Gzip level6 compresses the wire payload below the send buffers, so gzip is not a forced oversized encoded-tail workload.
Native production channelz/observability remains included. No validation or instrumentation is disabled to improve native results.

C8 is the immutable source-pinned baseline. C11 adds bounded idle decoded-buffer reuse with bounded initialization and the cold-short ordinary path; the benchmark and measurement interpretation are unchanged.
small-N diagnostic (25/50); setup subtraction and scheduling can dominate differences
native process CPU ticks and getrusage context switches are coarse scheduling diagnostics, not qualified speed claims
CPU tick N/2N deltas are coarse; nonpositive deltas stay unavailable
paired-ratio medians and ratios of medians are distinct and labelled separately
all source changes are combined; these counters do not establish individual causation
